newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa gears up for new Eastern Cape port project.
newsitem.headline: South Africa gears up for new Eastern Cape port project.

text.p: Billions of rands worth of investments hang in the balance as officials in South Africa's Eastern Cape step up preparations for their ambitious Coega Industrial Development Zone project.
They hope to receive the final go-ahead early in 1997 for the project, which could revitalise one of South Africa's poorest provinces and boost employment.
The brainchild of the Port Elizabeth municipality, the project centres around the building of a deep water industrial harbour in the mouth of the Coega River.
If this part of the project is realised, it will pave the way for the establishment of an industrial zone on 10,000 hectares of sandy, low-value farmland used mainly for grazing.

Port Elizabeth Municipality marketing manager Andre Crouse told Reuters that Gencor had already expressed interest in investing in a zinc refinery at Coega, which would pave the way for ancillary industries such as a fertiliser plant.
Pretoria Portland Cement Ltd (PPC) had expressed interest in building a cement plant and several other projects had been mooted, Crouse said.
"By March/April next year we have to secure Portnet approval for a port to be constructed, because if we do that we secure the zinc refinery," Crouse said.
The idea of a port of Coega was first mooted in 1972 but was dropped because of economic sanctions against the then apartheid South Africa.
Recently it was discussed with transport parastatal Transnet chairwoman Louise Tager who "immediately showed interest in the idea and that is where it started", Crouse said.
Since then an environmental study has been launched and various surveys and planning projects are in hand by electricity parastatal Eskom, Portnet and various investors, Crouse said.
Their findings are expected by March or April.
Crouse said that the government had shown strong support for the project.
"A project of this magnitude fits in with government's overall idea of strengthening our job creating abilities and the investment attraction ability of the area," Crouse.

Before South Africa broke off diplomatic ties with Taiwan, one of the largest potential investors was a Taiwanese group, which indicated that it wanted to build an aromatics petrochemical plant at Coega in a 50-50 joint venture with local companies. But it appears to have been shelved.
